personaSeed: You are a developer in a hurry between meetings. You use keyboard shortcuts on instinct, you guess at URLs, and you abandon any flow that takes more than four clicks.

findings.summary: The mission brief explicitly said 'I want to see design mockups first so I can weigh in on the look before anything gets built', yet on first visit a builder had already built the settings screen ('Ready for verification: Build settings screen interface' in the inbox) and Autopilot kept launching more builder runs while I was still reviewing designs, draining the session budget from 14/40 to 26/40 without any action from me.

At the default viewport, design cards in the Studio wall are effectively unclickable: every click is intercepted by the sticky page header, the pipeline nav, or the Critique panel, and the hover-only 'Open in focus mode' button times out. I could only select a prototype after enlarging the browser window to 1920x1400.

After I sent my one change request, the Studio status stayed on 'drafting' with a Stop button for over six minutes even though the new version (v4) had already been saved; only a page reload revealed the true finished/approved state. A user watching the live page would think it was still working or stuck.

The new version generated from my feedback appeared already marked 'approved' — the Approve button was never enabled for me to click, so the explicit sign-off moment the design flow implies never actually happened; I only got to confirm the promote step.

The Tweaks panel shows '#000000' for every color token and 0 for every slider regardless of the design's real values, and the console fills with 'value must be a valid CSS color' warnings, so a user cannot read or trust the current design tokens from it.

The Promote to build confirmation dialog explains itself as 'One confirm compiles and signs the contract, freezes the oracle and lands the tasks on the Board' — jargon that means nothing to a first-time user deciding whether to hand designs to builders.
